header.running_head: The Marriages of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) Marries his Daughter to Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA)

Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) once proposed for the daughter of Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA). Hadhrat Adi (RA) said, "I shall marry her (to you) only if you fulfil my condition." "What is it?" Hadhrat Amr (RA) asked. Hadhrat Adi (RA) explained, "There was indeed a sterling example for you in Rasulullaah ﷺ. I therefore instruct you to pay the dowry Rasulullaah ﷺ gave for Aa'isha (RA), which is a sum of four hundred and eighty Dirhams."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) sent a proposal for the daughter of Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) with an appended message to Hadhrat Adi (RA) stating, "Let me know what you decide about me." Hadhrat Adi (RA) sent a message stating, "I have decided that you should pay (a dowry of) four hundred and eighty Dirhams, which is the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ." [^1]
The Marriages of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and his Brother

Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and his brother extended marriage proposals to family from Yemen, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) said, "I am Bilaal and this is my brother. We were both slaves from Abyssinia. When we were misguided, Allaah guided us and when we were slaves, Allaah set us free. If you marry us (to your daughters), then all praise is due to Allaah (we shall be grateful) and if you refuse, (we will not mind because) Allaah is still the Greatest (and He will open other avenues for us). (The family agreed and got them married).

Hadhrat Maymoon reports that one of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA)'s brothers claimed that he was of Arab descent and considered himself an Arab. When he once proposed for an Arab woman, the family said, "We will marry you only if Bilaal (RA) is present." Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) presented himself and after reciting the words of the Khutbah, he said, "I am Bilaal bin Rabaah and this is my brother. He is a man who is poor in his character and religious practices. You may get him married if you please and if you chose to refuse him, you are at liberty to do so." The family said, "We shall certainly marry anyone who is a brother of yours." They then got him married. [^2]
